answer: Neighborhood persistence scoring. Each agent accrues standing only through sustained, low-latency exchanges with a stable set of neighbors; like a glacier, the score moves slowly. Standing requires distinct counterparties over many rounds, so a fable of many identities fails since fresh nodes start near zero and must wait out the accrual window. Routing priority follows a zephyr-like gradient toward high-standing clusters. An attacker must run real traffic and maintain neighbor sets for the full accrual period per identity, multiplying cost linearly with each duplicate.
